passage.text: The old lighthouse keeper climbed the spiral stairs every evening, counting each of the one hundred and twelve steps. He had done this for thirty-one years, through storms that rattled the glass and calm nights when the sea looked like polished stone. Tonight, though, something was different: a small boat drifted near the rocks, its lantern flickering. [sighs] He reached for the radio, hoping someone would answer before the tide turned. The radio crackled, and a tired voice answered from the harbor. Within minutes, two lights moved across the water toward the boat, and the keeper finally let out the breath he had been holding.

reference.text: We asked over twenty different people, and they all said it was his.
